blocks.text: Task: can pick, lift, transport, and place inside its assigned bin. Source embodiment A is the 7-DoF Franka Panda; target embodiment B is the 6-DoF UR5e. Both operate in headless robosuite/MuJoCo PickPlaceCan.

blocks.title: Claim boundary
blocks.text: This is a working simulation infrastructure baseline using oracle_sim_state. Source information is limited to grasp offset and lift clearance inside a hand-coded controller. No real-human-video inference, vision-only policy, full-motion transfer, or physical-robot transfer has been demonstrated.
Original runs: bootstrap_20261105T181834Z and fast_20261105T182127Z. Later review videos re-execute frozen policies; they do not introduce new policy training.

blocks.text: Three separate meanings of success

Teacher success is placement achieved by the executed source-grounded controller. Learned-policy success is placement achieved by the saved MLP in closed loop on different simulator seeds. Human-video understanding success would require actual CLIP and Qwen inference on a real human clip; it is currently untested.

The dataset source is human-operated Panda robot demonstration data, not a video of an unaided person. The executable Panda scripted branch validates live source control, while the new original-state source videos reconstruct recorded HDF5 states. These are distinct evidence types.

blocks.text: Contracts and units

JSON carries light metadata and provenance; NPZ carries typed trajectory arrays; CSV carries attempt/evaluation rows; MP4 supplies visual evidence. Positions are meters, times seconds, and angles radians. Named frames distinguish source_world, target_world, object_relative, and human_image_px.

The downloaded data include actions [T,7], EEF position [T,3], EEF quaternion [T,4], gripper observations, object state [T,14], simulator states [T,71], and an original model XML per episode. T varies by demonstration. No old learned robomimic checkpoint is loaded into the newer simulator.

pages.title: Data selection: what actually ran
pages.subtitle: Fast mode chooses five episodes from the first eight inspected source IDs; it does not search or rank the entire 200-episode corpus.

blocks.text: Deterministic selection algorithm

1. Enumerate source demos by numeric ID and inspect at most eight candidates (demo_0 through demo_7). Require nonempty actions and consistent observation lengths; retain the Can/Panda task provenance.
2. Sort coherent candidates by sample count, breaking ties by demo ID. Select the shortest demonstration first.
3. Repeatedly select the remaining candidate with the greatest minimum Euclidean initial-object-position distance to the already selected set. Stop after five selections.

selected = [shortest_consistent_demo]
while len(selected) < 5:
    next = argmax_d min_s ||object_start[d] - object_start[s]||_2
    selected.append(next)
Output and limitation

selection.json records all inspected shapes, selected IDs, initial positions, source file hash, reasons, and strategy. The observed source-selection method is a metadata baseline. It supplies reproducible diversity but does not demonstrate task-aware learned retrieval or optimal source selection.

blocks.text: Missing input is an auditable outcome

The recorded full run full_20261105T182257Z reports partial / requires_human_video. Step 2 has skipped_missing_input; retargeting and policy learning are skipped. Diagnosis records zero episodes and no feasible corrective iteration. A successful script exit or generated report does not imply human-video processing succeeded.

To validate this branch, supply a real clip with provenance and file hash; retain sampled frames, actual CLIP scores, Qwen prompt/raw text, parsed JSON, semantic mapping assumptions, and a human review of goal correctness. Then verify that the validated JSON gates the same downstream retargeting pipeline.

pages.title: Task understanding: provided semantics
pages.subtitle: Bootstrap and fast modes validate an explicit task specification; they do not infer goals from invented video.

blocks.text: Executed task representation

The seed contains eight ordered stages: pre-grasp, grasp, close, lift, transport, lower, open, and retreat. Constraints require lifting before transport, clearing the source bin wall, and releasing over the assigned target compartment. Pydantic rejects unsupported object/goal relations and fabricated known physical properties.

rows: Can object in PickPlaceCan. The object identity is fixed for this MVP.
The Can object's assigned target_bin_placements[can_index] entry. The visual receptacle in a future clip need not look identical.
Read from privileged simulator state; no metric 3D position is reconstructed from monocular video.
Mass / friction / contact in task JSON
Remain unknown. Simulator contact used by controller/features is a separate privileged observation, not an inferred human-video contact fact.

blocks.text: Interface to retargeting

task_spec.json includes schema version, seed, mode, task source, model/controller name, input IDs, units, privilege flags, semantic mapping, and assumptions. Stage 3 validates the task before collection and refuses unsupported semantic mappings. The controller still implements only the fixed can-inside-bin scenario; it is not a general task planner.

pages.title: What crosses the embodiment boundary
pages.subtitle: The source contribution is a measured grasp offset and lift clearance, not a copied joint trajectory or a learned source policy.

blocks.text: Schema discovery matters

For the actual 14D object observation, indices 0:7 contain EEF-relative pose; world can position is 7:10 and world quaternion is 10:14. Treating the first three values as world XYZ produces physically implausible geometry. The adapter explicitly decodes and tests this layout. EEF pose and actions are read from their named datasets. Timestamps are reconstructed from the recorded 20 Hz control rate.
Extraction and calibration

r[t] = eef_position[t] - can_world_position[t]
closing = {t : recorded_gripper_action[t] > 0}
grasp_t = argmin_t_in_closing ||r[t]||_2
grasp_offset = r[grasp_t]
source_lift = max_t can_z[t] - can_z[0]

When closing actions are absent, a geometric nearest-approach fallback is explicitly labeled. The target clips XY offsets to +/-25 mm and Z offset to [-15,40] mm. Lift is clipped to [0.12,0.25] m and combined with the configured minimum clearance. Object-relative axes remain world-aligned for the cylindrical can; this is a translation-relative construction, not a full rotating object-frame motion transfer.

blocks.title: Scientific limit / P02
blocks.text: The overall phase sequence, target generation, gripper timing, and orientation handling are hand-coded. Source quaternions may be stored, but their full time-varying orientation is not transferred. No source-parameter ablation has isolated the benefit of the source information.

blocks.text: The teacher action is normalized XYZ = clip(0.6 * (waypoint - EEF) / 0.05, -1, 1), with positive gripper closure during close through lower. The phase tracker is computed online from simulator observations and elapsed phase steps. It is shared with policy evaluation, making this a hybrid learned-controller system rather than an autonomous learned phase planner.
Executed outcomes and retained provenance

Fast mode executed one scripted Panda success and ten source-retargeted UR5e successes. Bootstrap executed one scripted Panda success and three source-retargeted UR5e successes. The separate target_scripted_bootstrap fallback had zero attempts in these runs; therefore no source-versus-oracle comparison was performed. Attempt rows retain seed, source ID, origin, placement error, lift, and failure code.

blocks.title: Code does not prove physical infeasibility / P05
blocks.text: The historical unreachable_waypoint label means an early waypoint was not reached by the horizon. It is not an IK infeasibility certificate. At failed learned-policy seed 10000, the teacher succeeds from the same initial features.

These produce 1,620 state-action rows; rows are temporally correlated samples from ten episodes, not 1,620 independent demonstrations. Bootstrap uses three episodes and 496 rows.

blocks.text: Filtering and separation

The dataset builder accepts success=true, robot=UR5e, and teacher_origin in {source_retargeted, target_scripted_bootstrap}. Failed episodes, Panda episodes, learned-policy review rollouts, and any episode whose seed overlaps held-out evaluation are excluded or rejected. A zero-success dataset yields blocked_insufficient_teacher_data instead of invented training arrays.

Normalization mean and standard deviation are fitted only on accepted training rows; standard deviation has a 0.001 floor. The same statistics are saved with the model. Per-episode origins, source IDs, seeds, sample counts, and paths remain in dataset_metadata.json.

blocks.title: Known conditioning gap / P06
blocks.text: Source-specific grasp offset, lift clearance, and the current waypoint are not explicit components of the 26D input. They vary across teachers; evaluation uses the first successful teacher's tracker parameters. The structural mismatch is verified, while its contribution to the failure remains a hypothesis.

pages.title: A small behavior-cloning model
pages.subtitle: The first learned target policy is deliberately low-dimensional; ACT, SmolVLA, and RGB policy learning are outside the executed baseline.

rows: 26 input features -> Linear 128 + ReLU -> Linear 128 + ReLU -> 4 outputs.
Three normalized XYZ regression values and one gripper logit. XYZ is clipped; logit >= 0 closes, otherwise opens.
Adam; learning rate 0.001; 2,000 updates; batch size 128; training seed 42; gradient norm clipped to 10.
Positive-class BCE weight = (# open / # close), clamped to [0.25,4]; computed only from training rows.
Model weights, model dimensions, optimizer, normalization, dataset provenance, step, CPU/CUDA/sampling RNG states.

blocks.text: Action adapter and units

The intermediary is not sent directly to robosuite. BASIC/OSC_POSE expects seven values: XYZ delta, three orientation deltas, and the gripper command. The adapter uses the installed composite controller's create_action_vector API, verifies 6D arm control and 7D environment action dimensions, inserts zero orientation deltas, and clips normalized values. Each XYZ unit maps to 0.05 m per control step in the tested controller.

Zero orientation delta holds the controller's initial orientation. BC does not learn orientation motion. Fresh-process evaluation loads the saved checkpoint and the same normalization and feature builder; training loss alone is never treated as task success.
Observed final losses: fast 0.000499 after 2,000 updates; bootstrap 0.002245 after 300 updates. These are fitting diagnostics, not independent control-performance measures.

pages.title: Actual closed-loop target performance
pages.subtitle: One shared baseline checkpoint is evaluated on simulator seeds 10000-10009; these seeds are excluded from teacher training.

blocks.text: What is measured

Each episode executes the learned XYZ/gripper outputs through the same action adapter and online phase tracker. The original goal predicate delegates to installed robosuite _check_success(). Mean placement error is the final can-to-target XY distance; it is not a full 3D pose/orientation score. Fast baseline success is 9/10; all-episode mean XY error is 81.55 mm, dominated by failed seed 10000. Success-only mean is 6.53 mm.
Stronger review predicate is separate / P09

Later review re-executes the frozen policy and checks the specific Can inside its assigned compartment, no grasp contact, and one additional second under the same policy. No scripted override assists the learned rollout. These stability annotations supplement rather than overwrite the original evaluation. Review videos and NPZ are excluded from training.

blocks.title: Evaluation limits / P07
blocks.text: Ten simulator seeds and one training seed do not establish broad generalization. The policy depends on exact simulator state and a manual phase tracker. No unseen object class, task family, camera estimator, physical robot, or perception robustness result is available.

blocks.text: failure_report.csv contains one row per analyzed episode with seed, teacher origin, step attribution, reason, XY error, lift/drop/release flags, diagnostic_oracle_used=true, confidence type, and evidence. Native task outcomes and deterministic rule-based interpretations are distinguished from unknowns.

feedback_requests.json ranks observed failure codes and suggests bounded experiments. The implemented automatic intervention is generic successful-teacher collection plus BC retraining. The failure-report language must not imply that a causal model selected a proven remedy.

blocks.text: Executed intervention

After observing learned-policy failures, select a feasible successful source-retargeted teacher origin, collect bounded additional trajectories on training seeds distinct from the evaluation set, merge successful data with the original teachers, retrain BC, and evaluate on the same held-out seeds. Baseline and corrective fast models each use 2,000 updates; bootstrap uses 300 updates. The intervention does not directly query or add the failed held-out trajectory to training.

The fast failure at seed 10000 remains. A bootstrap failure at seed 10002 changes to a stable reviewed success. Additional data and retraining have not been isolated using a retraining-only control. The already-inspected held-out seeds are appropriate for a debugging before/after comparison, while final method selection requires a separate untouched evaluation set.

pages.title: The persistent pregrasp stall
pages.subtitle: Observed behavior is specific; the root cause remains unresolved.

rows: No reported collision in review evidence
No reported collision in review evidence

blocks.text: The source-grounded teacher succeeds from the same initial features. Therefore the learned failure does not demonstrate an unreachable physical target. The policy approaches but settles outside the phase transition threshold, so no subsequent grasp/lift sequence begins. Both checkpoints show this symptom.
Two testable hypotheses, not established causes

Conditioning mismatch: five teacher-specific grasp/clearance settings are pooled, but the policy input does not explicitly include those parameters or the waypoint. Evaluation uses one fixed parameter set.
Distribution shift: initial object_x and goal_minus_object_x are outside the full training feature range in the reviewed failure; the largest initial absolute z-score is 7.55 on object_minus_eef_y. Range/z-score observations alone do not establish causality.

blocks.title: Next controlled comparison
blocks.text: Compare fixed-parameter teachers, parameter-conditioned BC, and the existing mixed-teacher baseline at equal training budget. Log waypoint error, XYZ outputs, normalized features, and phase transitions over time. Keep seed 10000 as a regression case; evaluate final gains on new untouched seeds and multiple training seeds.

blocks.text: The source HDF5 records robosuite 1.5.1, while the current simulator is 1.5.2. Reusing original XML and numerically checking reconstructed Can/EEF positions is therefore an explicit compatibility step. A successful state reconstruction does not prove that replaying the recorded actions under newer physics reproduces the same dynamics or task success.

All recorded source frames pass the 1e-8 m position tolerance. Source clips visualize stored successful demonstrations (terminal reward=1, done=1 for demo_3/5/7); they do not validate execution of the old actions under new dynamics.

pages.title: SSH-safe runs and exact artifacts
pages.subtitle: The runnable baseline is detached; report and media generation do not replace actual training/evaluation evidence.

blocks.text:
cd /home/dheo/Cross_Robot_Real2Sim
bash scripts/setup.sh
bash scripts/preflight.sh
bash scripts/launch.sh bootstrap
bash scripts/status.sh RUN_ID
tail -f runs/RUN_ID/logs/pipeline.log
bash scripts/resume.sh bootstrap RUN_ID
bash scripts/stop.sh RUN_ID

launch.sh creates a detached tmux session with absolute project paths, activates the project environment inside it, exports CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 and EGL settings, and stores run/session/PID metadata. Logs include timestamps. A project GPU lock prevents unintended concurrent project launches. tmux survives SSH/VS Code disconnection while the host stays running; it is not host-reboot persistence.

The supervisor uses pipefail so tee does not hide a failed pipeline, records an exit code, handles signals, and preserves artifacts for resumption. Status checks both live process/session identity and persisted outcomes; disappearance alone never means success. Resume validates frozen configuration, input/artifact hashes, JSON/NPZ/checkpoint readability, and seed splits.
Dependency and artifact reproduction

bash scripts/launch.sh fast
# Real human input later:
cp /path/to/real_human_can_clip.mp4 data/human/
bash scripts/setup.sh full
bash scripts/launch.sh full
# Rebuild this PDF, without retraining:
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-report.txt
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_english_report.py

Simulation, optional perception, review plotting, and PDF dependencies have separate requirement files. Original environment snapshots and lockfiles remain historical evidence. Raw runs/checkpoints/datasets stay local and gitignored; compact metrics, manifests, selected videos, and this report are versioned.

pages.subtitle: The evidence supports an honest baseline and specific next experiments, not an already-complete general real-to-sim method.

blocks.text: A prioritized experimental sequence

First: resolve the pregrasp stall with equal-budget fixed-parameter versus parameter-conditioned policies, plus a retraining-only control.
Second: isolate source-information value with source-on/source-off/mismatched-source ablations under matched target starts.
Third: validate real human input end to end and only then expand evaluation seeds, training seeds, state-estimation conditions, and physical-robot claims.
